pmkisan.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a Central Sector Scheme launched in February 2019 to provide income support to all landholding farmer families across the country. The scheme provides financial assistance directly to farmers to supplement their financial needs for procuring inputs to ensure proper crop health and yields.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Financial benefit of ₹6,000 per year is provided in three equal installments of ₹2,000 each, every four months (April-July, August-November, December-March). The amount is directly transferred to the bank account of the beneficiary farmer via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All landholding farmer families with cultivable land are eligible, subject to certain exclusion criteria. Excluded categories include: income tax payers, institutional landholders, constitutional post holders, serving/retired government employees, professionals such as doctors, engineers, lawyers, and chartered accountants with annual income above ₹10,000.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Farmers can register through: (1) PM-KISAN portal at pmkisan.gov.in, (2) Common Service Centres (CSC) with a fee of ₹30, (3) State/UT government nodal officers, (4) Local Patwari/Revenue Officer/Nodal Officer of State Government. Aadhaar-based verification is mandatory.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Aadhaar card (mandatory for authentication), land ownership/cultivable land records (Khasra, Patta or equivalent), bank account details linked to Aadhaar, citizenship proof.

shc.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: The Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme was launched in February 2015 under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA). Under this scheme, the Government of India provides every farmer a Soil Health Card once in every two years, which carries crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilizers required for individual farms to help farmers improve productivity through judicious use of inputs.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Free soil testing of agricultural land every two years. Crop-wise recommendations for macronutrients (N, P, K) and micronutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, S). Personalized fertilizer advice to improve yields and reduce input costs. Helps in improved soil management leading to better farm productivity.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All farmers with agricultural land are eligible. The scheme covers farmers in all states and union territories across India. Priority is given to farmers who have not had their soil tested before and those in soil-deficient areas.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Farmers can get their soil tested by: (1) Contacting the local agriculture department office or Soil Testing Laboratory (STL), (2) Approaching the nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), (3) Applying through Common Service Centres (CSC) in some states, (4) Through State Agriculture Department mobile units that visit villages. The card is issued within 30 days of sample collection.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Aadhaar card, land records (Khasra number/Patta), contact information. No fee is charged for soil testing under this scheme.

pmfby.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) was launched in January 2016 as a comprehensive crop insurance scheme replacing the earlier National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS). It provides financial support to farmers suffering crop loss or damage due to unforeseen events like natural calamities, pests, and diseases.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Coverage for crop losses due to non-preventable natural risks, prevented sowing, post-harvest losses, and localized calamities. Premium rates are very low: 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops. Government pays the balance premium. Sum insured based on Scale of Finance declared by the state. Claims settled within 2 months of harvest.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing notified crops in notified areas are eligible. Both loanee farmers (mandatory coverage for those with crop loans from banks) and non-loanee farmers (voluntary) can enrol. Aadhaar is mandatory for registration.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Loanee farmers are enrolled automatically by their bank at time of crop loan. Non-loanee farmers can apply through: (1) Banks (nationalised, cooperative, Regional Rural Banks), (2) Common Service Centres (CSC), (3) Insurance company agents, (4) Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana portal (pmfby.gov.in). Applications must be submitted before the cutoff date for each season.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Aadhaar card, land records or lease agreement (for tenant farmers), bank account details, crop sowing certificate from Patwari/Agriculture Officer, photograph of standing crop before loss (for post-harvest claims).

kcc.provider_name: Department of Financial Services, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme was introduced in 1998 to meet the short-term credit requirements of farmers for cultivation, post-harvest expenses, maintenance of farm assets, and allied activities. It was revamped in 2012 to also cover allied and non-farm activities of farmers and fishermen. The scheme provides affordable credit at 7% p.a. with 3% interest subvention for timely repayment.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Revolving credit limit up to ₹3 lakh for crop cultivation at 7% interest rate; effective rate of 4% with 3% subvention for prompt repayment. Credit limit of ₹1.60 lakh without margin and collateral. Covers crop cultivation expenses, post-harvest expenses, produce marketing, maintenance of farm assets, allied activities, and consumption requirements. Personal accident insurance cover of ₹50,000.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: Eligible applicants include: (1) Individual or joint borrowers who are owner-cultivators, (2) Tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers, (3) Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers including tenant farmers/sharecroppers. Minimum age: 18 years; Maximum age: 75 years (above 60: co-borrower required).

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Apply at: (1) Any Scheduled Commercial Bank, Regional Rural Bank (RRB), or Cooperative Bank branch near your area, (2) Online through the bank's internet banking portal, (3) Common Service Centres (CSC) linked to banks. Fill the KCC application form and submit with required documents. Loan is usually sanctioned within 7-14 working days.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Duly filled KCC application form, two recent passport-size photographs, identity proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID/PAN), address proof, land records (Khasra/Khatauni/Patta), crop details (type, area under cultivation), income proof, any existing loan account details.

pmksy.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was launched in 2015 with the motto 'Har Khet Ko Pani, More Crop Per Drop'. It aims to achieve convergence of investments in irrigation at the field level, expand cultivable area under assured irrigation, improve on-farm water use efficiency, introduce sustainable water conservation practices, and ensure end-to-end solution for farm water supply and use.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Subsidy on micro-irrigation systems: 55% for small and marginal farmers, 45% for other farmers. Under Per Drop More Crop (PDMC): drip irrigation, sprinkler systems, secondary storage structures, water-carrying pipes. Enhanced crop productivity and reduction in water usage by 40-50%. Components include Har Khet Ko Pani (surface irrigation), PDMC (micro-irrigation), and Watershed Development.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All farmers owning agricultural land are eligible. Priority given to small and marginal farmers (land holding up to 2 ha), Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes. For micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler): minimum 0.5 acre land holding required. Beneficiary should not have availed subsidy under the scheme in the last 7 years for the same land parcel.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Apply through: (1) State Agriculture/Horticulture Department, (2) District Agriculture Officer (DAO) / District Horticulture Officer (DHO), (3) State government online portals for PMKSY. Applications accepted before sowing season. Physical inspection of land by agriculture officer required before subsidy release.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Land records (Khasra, Patta), Aadhaar card, recent passport-size photographs, bank account details, quotation from empanelled vendor for micro-irrigation equipment, caste certificate (for SC/ST farmers), water source availability certificate.

sathi.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: SATHI (Seed Authentication, Traceability and Holistic Inventory) is a digital platform developed by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare to ensure availability of quality seeds to farmers by tracking seeds from production to purchase through QR-code-based authentication, preventing counterfeit seeds from reaching farmers.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Ensures farmers receive certified quality seeds. QR-code based seed packet authentication via mobile app. Traceability of seeds from producer to retailer to farmer. Access to subsidized certified seeds. Prevents counterfeit seed sales. Farmers can verify seed authenticity instantly at point of purchase.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All farmers registered on the SATHI portal or with their State Agriculture Department are eligible. Seeds of notified varieties of food crops, vegetables, flowers, and other agricultural commodities are covered. Registered dealers and seed agencies are mandatory participants.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Download the SATHI mobile application from the App Store/Play Store. Register with your farmer ID / Aadhaar. Scan the QR code on seed packets before purchase to verify authenticity. Access subsidized certified seeds through registered dealers. Grievance filing for counterfeit seeds available on the portal.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Farmer registration number or Aadhaar card for SATHI portal registration. No additional documentation required for seed verification. For subsidy on seeds: land records, bank account details.

pmasha.short_desc: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan
pmasha.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-ASHA) is an umbrella scheme launched in 2018 to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their produce. It comprises three sub-schemes: Price Support Scheme (PSS), Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS), and Pilot of Private Procurement and Stockist Scheme (PPPS).

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Price Support Scheme (PSS): Physical procurement of oilseeds, pulses, copra at MSP by government agencies. Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS): Direct payment of difference between MSP and market price to registered farmers without physical procurement. Private Procurement Stockist Scheme (PPPS): Up to 15% of state production covered through private agencies with government backstop.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All farmers growing notified oilseeds, pulses, and copra in states where the scheme is operational are eligible. For PDPS: farmers must register in advance on the portal with land and bank details. MSP procurement is available for notified crops during the procurement season in designated mandis.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Register on the PM-ASHA portal with state government. Approach designated procurement centres (NAFED, FCI, state agencies) during harvest season. For PDPS: register online before crop harvest with details of acreage, expected production. Bring produce with sale slip to procurement centre during notified period.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Aadhaar card, land records and sowing certificate, bank account details (linked to Aadhaar), crop registration on PM-ASHA portal (for PDPS). Sell slip or token from mandi to be produced at procurement centre.

aif.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) is a medium-long term debt financing facility launched in 2020 to fund viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets. It provides ₹1 lakh crore worth of loans at concessional interest rates to promote investment in agriculture infrastructure at farm gate and aggregation points.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Interest subvention of 3% per annum on loans up to ₹2 crore for eligible entities. Credit guarantee support through Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) for loans up to ₹2 crore. Eligible activities include cold storage, warehouses, silos, sorting-grading units, assaying units, primary processing centres, ripening chambers, logistics facilities.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: Eligible entities include: Farmers (individually or as JLGs/FPOs), Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Marketing Cooperative Societies, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), SHGs, Agri-entrepreneurs, Startups, Central/State agency or Local Body sponsored Public Private Partnership projects.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Apply online through the AIF portal (agriinfra.dac.gov.in). Create account, fill project details, upload required documents, submit application. Application reviewed by empanelled banks/NBFCs/Cooperative Banks. Loan sanctioned within 60 days of complete application. Can also apply directly at any empanelled financial institution.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Project report with financial projections, land ownership/lease documents, entity registration documents (for cooperatives/FPOs), bank account details, income tax returns (last 3 years for established entities), quotations for proposed infrastructure, collateral documents (if applicable).

smam.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme to accelerate the growth of farm mechanization in the country, especially in small farm sector, to reach out to regions and segments of farming where farm power availability is low, and to promote 'custom hiring' of farm machinery to offset disadvantage of high costs of individual ownership among small and marginal farmers.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Financial assistance (subsidy) on purchase of farm machinery and equipment: 40-50% subsidy for general category farmers; up to 50% for SC/ST and women farmers. Establishment of Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) and Farm Machinery Banks with up to 40% (max ₹12 lakh) subsidy. High-Tech Hub subsidy up to 40% (max ₹20 lakh). In-situ crop residue management machinery: 50% subsidy to individual farmers, 80% to CHCs.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All categories of farmers are eligible. Priority given to small and marginal farmers, SC/ST farmers, and women farmers who get higher subsidy rates. For Custom Hiring Centres: any farmer group, cooperative, FPO, or entrepreneur can apply. Beneficiary should not have availed subsidy on the same type of machinery in the last 5-7 years (state-specific norms).

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Apply through: (1) State Agriculture Department's online portal (most states have e-applications), (2) District Agriculture Office, (3) Sub-district / Block Agriculture Office. Apply before purchasing machinery. Pre-approval from the department is necessary before purchasing the subsidized equipment. Lottery system used in case of excess applications in many states.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Aadhaar card, land records, bank account details, recent photographs, category certificate (for SC/ST/women farmers), quotation from authorised dealer, registration certificate of existing tractors (if applicable for tractor-linked implements).

pdmc.short_desc: Per Drop More Crop — Micro Irrigation
pdmc.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) is a component of PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) focused exclusively on micro-irrigation — drip and sprinkler systems — to enhance water use efficiency at the farm level. The scheme promotes efficient on-farm water management practices and reduces water wastage while improving crop productivity.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Subsidy on drip irrigation systems: 55% for small/marginal farmers (land ≤ 2 ha), 45% for other farmers. Subsidy on sprinkler systems: 55% for small/marginal, 45% for others. Water savings of 40-50% compared to flood irrigation. Yield improvement of 20-50% depending on crop. Also covers secondary storage structures, water-carrying pipes, and fertigation equipment.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: All farmers with a minimum of 0.5 acre of agricultural land. Farmers with access to a reliable water source (borewell, canal, river, tank). One-time benefit per farmer per land parcel (subsidy not available if availed within last 7 years). SC/ST and women farmers may get additional state-level benefits.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Apply through: (1) District Agriculture/Horticulture Office, (2) State government PMKSY-PDMC portal, (3) Registered drip/sprinkler equipment manufacturers/dealers. Select empanelled vendor, get installation quote. Submit application with documents. After approval, purchase and install system. Subsidy released after field verification.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Land records (Khasra number, area), Aadhaar card, bank account details, quotation from empanelled/registered vendor, water source availability proof (borewell registration / water permission), geo-tagged photograph of field, caste certificate (for SC/ST farmers).

pkvy.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) was launched in 2015 under NMSA to promote organic farming in India through a cluster approach. The scheme encourages traditional and indigenous organic farming methods and helps farmers adopt organic farming practices, reduce dependence on chemical inputs, and access premium organic markets.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare for 3 years to farmer clusters: ₹31,000 for organic input procurement, ₹8,800 for capacity building and training, ₹3,000 for certification (PGS-India), ₹7,200 for value addition and marketing. Cluster-based certification through Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India). Access to organic market linkages and premium prices.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: Farmers must organise themselves in clusters of minimum 20 farmers covering minimum 20 acres (10 ha) of contiguous land. All farmers in the cluster must commit to adopting organic farming practices. Land must have been under chemical-free farming for at least 3 years (conversion period). SC/ST farmers and women-led clusters are given priority.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Form a farmer cluster of 20+ farmers with 20+ acres. Approach the District Agriculture Officer (DAO) to register the cluster. Identify a Local Group (LG) resource person for guidance. Develop a 3-year organic farming plan with the help of DAO. Apply through State Agriculture Department PKVY portal. Certification through PGS-India will begin after cluster registration.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Individual land records of all cluster farmers, Aadhaar cards of all farmers, cluster registration application signed by all members, village map showing contiguous land parcels, declaration of chemical-free farming, details of Local Group (LG) representative, bank accounts of all farmer members.

nfsm.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: National Food Security Mission (NFSM) was launched in 2007-08 to increase production and productivity of rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals (maize, nutri-cereals), and commercial crops (cotton, jute, sugarcane) through area expansion and productivity enhancement in a sustainable manner. The scheme aims at restoring soil fertility and productivity and creating employment opportunities.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Subsidized certified seeds of high-yielding varieties (HYV) and hybrids (50% of seed cost). Subsidy on farm machinery (seed drills, zero-till seed-cum-fertilizer drills, rotavators, etc.) — up to 50% cost. Demonstrations on cluster basis for improved crop management practices. Soil amendments (lime/liming material) and micronutrients at subsidized rates. Integrated Pest Management (IPM) demonstrations.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: Farmers in identified districts/blocks growing NFSM-notified crops are eligible. The mission covers districts with low productivity and scope for enhancement. Priority to small and marginal farmers. Beneficiaries selected by State Agriculture Departments as per district action plans. Aadhaar and land records required for individual farmer benefits.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Apply through: (1) Block Agriculture Office (BAO) in your area, (2) District Agriculture Office, (3) State Agriculture Department portal in select states. Apply before the crop season (Kharif: April-May; Rabi: September-October). Benefits disbursed through input agencies or directly to farmer accounts via DBT for seed and machinery subsidies.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Aadhaar card, land records (Khasra/Patta showing the crop to be grown), bank account details, recent passport-size photograph, category certificate (for SC/ST preference), crop sowing certificate (for machinery subsidy claiming after sowing).

rad.provider_name: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

tags.name: Introduction
tags.value: Rainfed Area Development (RAD) is a sub-scheme under NMSA that promotes an Integrated Farming System (IFS) in rainfed areas to enhance farm income, improve resource use efficiency, and build resilience to climate variability. It focuses on developing farming systems that integrate crops with livestock, horticulture, fisheries, and forestry for improved livelihoods of small and marginal farmers.

tags.name: Benefits
tags.value: Support for Integrated Farming System (IFS) components: horticulture, livestock, poultry, fishery, apiculture, etc. — up to ₹36,000/ha. Water harvesting and management: farm ponds, water harvesting structures — up to ₹28,500/ha. Cluster demonstrations on IFS models. Capacity building and training. Value chain support for IFS produce. Focus on reducing crop risk through diversification.

tags.name: Eligibility
tags.value: Small and marginal farmers (land holding ≤ 2 ha) in rainfed and drought-prone districts notified under RAD. Farmers in rain-shadow areas and degraded land zones. Clusters of farmers organised in villages/hamlets for IFS demonstrations. Priority to women farmers and SC/ST communities. Beneficiary selection done by District Agriculture Office.

tags.name: How to Apply
tags.value: Apply through: (1) District Agriculture Office (DAO) in RAD-notified districts, (2) Block Agriculture Office, (3) Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) for technical guidance. Identify IFS components suitable for your land and water availability. Prepare a farm development plan with KVK/DAO support. Apply before the crop season for current year's assistance.

tags.name: Documents Required
tags.value: Land records (for small/marginal farmer classification), Aadhaar card, bank account details, proposed IFS plan details, water source information, category certificate (for SC/ST/women), recent photographs of farm land, any existing livestock/pond registration if applicable.
